requirements.evidence: All requirements and the contract are present: default map and range fallback (app/Models/Queue.php:24,36-42), custom map wins (Queue.php:49-51), canonical-key/letter/uniqueness validation on every save (Queue.php:67-96 plus saving hook at :28), per-prefix/per-day max+1 with malformed-code skipping and legacy A exclusion (app/Models/Ticket.php:36-51), issue_date cast (Ticket.php:130), one clock read for code day/issued_at/issue_date (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:42-59), nullable->backfill->NOT NULL plus index swap and down() (database/migrations/2026_10_29_040712_add_issue_date_to_tickets_table.php:18-42), factory alignment and priority/day allocation (database/factories/TicketFactory.php:42,48-55), UpdateQueue null/[]/set semantics with ValidationException (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:24,29-34,70-73), and docs (docs/business-rules.md:117, docs/database-schema.md:157-158, CHANGELOG.md:12,17).

conventions.evidence: Domain writes stay in App\Actions (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:18-25, app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:41-59); both new migrations define a down() (database/migrations/2026_10_29_040711_add_priority_prefix_map_to_queues_table.php:24-29, database/migrations/2026_10_29_040712_add_issue_date_to_tickets_table.php:39-45); the map is deliberately excluded from #[Fillable] (app/Models/Queue.php:12) with a mass-assignment test; public methods have PHPDoc (Queue.php:20-22,33-35,45-66; Ticket.php:25-35); docs are kept in sync; new tests use Pest and match sibling test style.

security.evidence: Reverification: authorization still runs first via Gate::forUser($actor)->authorize('update', $queue) (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:26), before the map is validated or assigned; all map input is validated server-side (app/Models/Queue.php:73-93) and enforced on every save (:28-30); the attribute is not mass-assignable (Queue.php:12, tests/Feature/QueuePriorityPrefixTest.php:70-76); an unauthorized-map-change test exists (tests/Feature/UpdateQueuePriorityPrefixMapTest.php:80-93); no new Blade output, secrets or client-trusted parameters were introduced.

tests.evidence: Broad Pest coverage: defaults/range/custom/fallback (tests/Feature/QueuePriorityPrefixTest.php:8-59), canonical keys, bad letters, uniqueness, empty-map normalization and validate-on-every-save (QueuePriorityPrefixTest.php:70-114), daily per-prefix sequencing, malformed and legacy codes, past-999, independent prefixes, midnight alignment and custom prefix issuance (tests/Feature/TicketDailyCodeTest.php:10-96), factory issue_date/priority/day/explicit-code behaviour (TicketDailyCodeTest.php:122-148), and UpdateQueue null/[]/invalid/authorization (tests/Feature/UpdateQueuePriorityPrefixMapTest.php:24-93). The only uncovered behaviour is the migration itself: the DATE(issued_at) backfill and down() are never exercised (database/migrations/2026_10_29_040712_add_issue_date_to_tickets_table.php:24,39).

simplicity.evidence: The implementation is small and reuses the existing model/action/factory paths (app/Models/Queue.php:24-96, app/Models/Ticket.php:36-51, app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:29-34). One redundancy: the map is normalized once in the action (UpdateQueue.php:31) with the result discarded, then the raw value is assigned (:72) and normalized again by the model hook (Queue.php:28), so every map save performs the validation loop twice.

readability.evidence: Clear names and focused methods (Queue::defaultPrefixFor, prefixForPriority, normalizePrefixMap at app/Models/Queue.php:36-96), concise docblocks explaining the daily scope and malformed-code skipping (app/Models/Ticket.php:25-35), and inline comments explaining the single clock read (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:41) and the intended leaving queue unchanged (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:28). No dead code, debug output or inconsistent style.

scope.evidence: Every edit serves the ticket: Queue/Ticket models, IssueTicket/UpdateQueue actions, factory, two migrations, CHANGELOG/business-rules/database-schema docs, and focused tests. The small docs/api/totem.md example update (A012 -> P012) documents the new code format rather than changing the API; no unrelated refactors or features.

issues.explanation: The action calls Queue::normalizePrefixMap() but discards the normalized result, then assigns the raw map at line 72 and normalizes it again in the model's saving hook (app/Models/Queue.php:28), so each save runs the validation/uniqueness loop twice; assigning the normalized array would keep the every-save guarantee with one pass.

The DATE(issued_at) backfill and the down() path are not covered by any test; RefreshDatabase only runs up() against an empty table, so the requirement that pre-existing rows are backfilled and that the migration reverses is unverified.

Because normalizePrefixMap() returns the raw PHP array and the attribute is cast straight to JSON, a valid map with sequential keys such as ['0' => 'X'] (or ['0' => 'X', '1' => 'Y']) is persisted as a JSON list (["X"]) rather than the JSON object documented at docs/database-schema.md:158; it still decodes to the same PHP map, so this is a shape/consistency nit only.

review.summary: The change implements priority-based N/P/E ticket prefixes with a validated per-queue JSON override, daily per-prefix sequences backed by a new tickets.issue_date column and (queue_id, code, issue_date) unique index, plus the UpdateQueue plumbing, factory support, docs and extensive Pest coverage. The main path and the specified edge cases (malformed/legacy codes, midnight, map validation, authorization, daily restart) are handled well; only minor items remain: a redundant second normalization pass, untested migration backfill/down(), and a nit about a JSON list being stored where the docs describe an object.
